title: Imputation Anchors and Signal Prioritization - scratch notes
content:
Context: scribbling out a practical approach to filling missing attribute values during ingestion and label cleanup. The goal is not to invent perfect ML models yet, but to establish robust, auditable heuristics that are: 1) fast to run in pipelines, 2) easy to explain to downstream consumers, and 3) have measurable fallbacks and confidence wiring for human review.

High-level constraints / desiderata:
- Preserve provenance: every imputed cell must carry an "imputation_reason" and minimal evidence pointers (e.g., sku pattern, other field, prior label).
- Avoid cascading false confidence: if an upstream imputation is later changed, downstream derived fields should be flagged for re-evaluation (not silently overwritten).
- Prefer precision > recall for imputation used for product-facing attributes (category, brand). For auxiliary attributes (has_free_shipping boolean) we can be more permissive.
- Keep heuristics interpretable and fallback to abstain for low-evidence cases.

Anchors (signals ranked by trust):
1) explicit labelled fields on same row (brand, category) - trust high
2) SKU regex groups + vendor mapping (if SKU contains vendor code) - trust medium-high after mapping table verification
3) normalized product title tokens (title -> ngrams -> vote) - trust medium (depends on token cleaning)
4) previous catalog entries (dedupe by normalized title or hash) - trust variable (stale catalog risk)
5) image-derived labels (if available, quick CNN tag) - trust medium but should be treated separately and surfaced as "vision_suggested"
6) inferred from seller metadata / merchant landing page - low-medium (external fetch failures common)

Practical rules (working list):
- Category imputation rule set:
  * If category empty and sku matches ^([A-Z]{3})-([0-9]{4})-.* then map group1 via sku_vendor_map. If vendor known and vendor->default_category exists, set category to that with reason=sku-vendor-default and confidence=0.75.
  * Else if title contains token matching curated category aliases (e.g., "running shoes", "sneakers") then set category with reason=title-ngram and confidence=0.6 if single strong match, 0.4 if multiple weak matches.
  * Else if previous_catalog.has(title_hash) then set category=previous_catalog[title_hash].category with reason=catalog-lookup, confidence=0.8, but mark source_age=years since catalog entry. If source_age > 2 years, cap confidence at 0.5.
  * Else abstain (empty) and enqueue for micro-sampling for human review.

- Brand: prioritize explicit "brand" field > merchant profile > normalized title token first word. If multiple signals conflict, choose explicit field; if explicit absent and merchant profile suspect (low trust), prefer abstain.

- Price currency: if currency missing and price > 1000 assume price is local-currency? No. This is too brittle. Rule: use seller_country -> default_currency map; if seller_country missing, infer currency from sku suffix (if matches pattern) otherwise leave blank and mark for sync.

Confidence wiring and provenance: 
- Each imputed field should produce a small provenance tuple stored as a string blob: "reason=sku-vendor-default;evidence=sku=ABC-1234;confidence=0.75;lookup_id=sku_map_v2". Keep all keys flat and short.
- Add top-level column imputation_level: {auto_high, auto_low, human_verified, abstain}. auto_high = heuristic with >=0.75 confidence and single-signal strong anchor. auto_low = >=0.4 and <0.75.
- When downstream features are derived (e.g., category -> category_bucket), add 'derived_from' pointer to origin field name and origin imputation_level to support recompute triggers.

Edge case notes / examples:
- Title: "King's Cross 3-in-1 kettle" -> apostrophes cause tokenizer splits, sometimes produce brand token 'King'. Shouldn't auto-assign "King" as brand unless other evidence exists. Rule: require title-brand match only when title-first-token is capitalized AND appears in merchant profile or known-brand-list.

- SKU collisions: same SKU across merchants with different categories. Use (merchant_id, sku) composite key for mapping; fallback to normalized title matching if merchant_id missing. Log a collision event for product ops review.

- Multi-item bundles: titles like "Socks 6-pack - assorted colors" should map category->apparel, but brand often "assorted" or empty. Don't create brand from color token; set brand blank and set imputation_reason=bundle-detection. Bundle detection heuristic: tokens like "pack", "bundle", "assorted", count>=1 and quantity_regex detected.

Sampling & audit:
- Daily micro-sample pipeline: pick 250 auto_high and 250 auto_low imputed rows across random merchants stratified by confidence and tag (category/brand/price). Push to a small human batch for quick accept/reject and capture error taxonomy (wrong_category, wrong_brand, stale_mapping, false_positive_bundle).
- Maintain rolling 30-day precision metric for each rule (sku-vendor-default, title-ngram, catalog-lookup). If precision(auto_high) < 0.9 for any rule, disable that rule and push a ticket.

Quick experiments to run (A/B style):
- Experiment A: title-ngram threshold 0.6 vs 0.7; measure downstream category-related regression in search CTR over 2 weeks.
- Experiment B: include image-suggested tag as tiebreaker for category when title and sku disagree; measure precision on micro-sample.

Short checklist for implementation:
- [ ] Add imputation_reason and imputation_blob columns to staging schema (flat string).
- [ ] Implement sku_vendor_map with provenance (who edited, version).
- [ ] Add auto_level rules and consistent confidence range usage across pipelines.
- [ ] Micro-sampling job + simple UI for labelers to mark errors and pick taxonomy.
- [ ] Alert rule: if daily auto_high precision falls >= 5% from baseline trigger ops.

Open questions / TODOs for syncing with Noah / Diego:
- Decide final format for imputation_blob (compact key=value; separator=| or ;?). My vote: semicolon-separated for readability but annotate in spec.
- How much of the "source_age" logic should be backfilled into historical rows? (Noah thinks yes, Diego cautious about compute cost)
- Risk: merchant profile scraping delays causing flapping brand imputations. Proposed: cache merchant_profile for 24h and mark as stale after 24h. Good?

Notes to self: keep this as small, auditable heuristics first pass. We can layer ML model later if rules start to fail at scale. For now, prioritize clear provenance and sampling so ops can revert or refine quickly.

Examples (compact):
row1 | title:"Ultralight Trail Runner - blue" | sku:"TRL-2345-UK" | merchant: "TrailCo" | brand:"" -> sku pattern anchor -> sku_vendor_map[TRL]=TrailCo -> brand=TrailCo (reason=sku-vendor-default;conf=0.75)
row2 | title:"6-pack ankle socks assorted" | sku:"SCK-6001" | brand:"" -> detect bundle -> brand="";category=apparel (reason=bundle-detection;conf=0.6)
row3 | title:"Vintage Oak Writing Desk" | sku:"" | brand:"Oak & Co" -> explicit brand present -> keep and mark human_verified if verified by merchant profile.

End notes: keep log of disabled rules and experiments in the linked github playbooks file. Update spec after first 2 weeks of sampling.
